messages:
alice: @here quick heads-up — Sparrow Labs wants a short POC. They have a 30B open model (they call it 'sparrow-30b-v1') and asked two parallel things: model catalog fit/variant compatibility + enterprise preflight (KMS, VPC, audit retention). Also asked for a rough Dedicated vs Hosted price estimate for ~200k tokens/day. Can eng-ml + infra weigh in?

raju: Do we know format of weights? HF/transformers tarball or custom? Also does model use rotary vs absolute pos emb? KV-cache friendliness matters for latency at 256 tokens.

alice: They said "HF-style weights + tokenizer.json" in the questionnaire. I'm attaching the short security Q later.

marta: OK. HF-style is good. Quick notes: - If tokenizer matches a model we already have, easier. - Quantization candidates: q4_0 / q4_k likely work, but we need a scan to verify layer types. - Runtime fallback to 13B is possible if we onboard a compatible 13B variant, but results will shift (recommend evals).

liam: From infra/security side: Private (VPC) + KMS integration = supported. We can stream audit logs to customer S3 with lifecycle policy for 1yr retention. For Private on-prem with HSM we need a field ops runbook.

alice: Customer asked whether we can hit p95 ~80ms at 256 tokens on Dedicated. Any ballpark?

marta: Realistic: on A100-like nodes, a non-quantized 30B at 256 tokens is usually ~100–160ms p95 depending on kernels and batch. With quantization + KV cache + continuous batching you can approach 60–90ms p95. So 80ms is possible but not guaranteed out-of-the-box. We should run a perf scan.

raju: Also confirm streaming + function-calling are supported for that model? Some model tops out on logits-only. If they need structured output we should validate.

marta: We'll run compatibility + perf scan. Command I'll run: ```
redwood model-scan --source /shared/sparrow-weights/ --format hf --out /tmp/sparrow-report.json
```
Expect: tokenizer check, layer types, attention kernel mapping, candidate qprofiles.

liam: For Dedicated pricing: rough guidance to share externally (high-level only): Hosted is simpler (no infra commit) but unit cost higher; Dedicated commit depends on target throughput and SLOs. For 200k tokens/day guess: hosted monthly bill ~low-to-mid thousands; Dedicated commit likely in low-to-mid tens of thousands depending on headroom. I'll DM a more careful tuck.

alice: Good enough for initial convo. Also they flagged licensing: they say weights are "customer-provided, permissive license" — sales worried about ingestion & redistributing. Legal/OS policy already says we can serve CPW (customer-provided weights) if license allows.

marta: Two operational asks from my side: 1) put the model and a 13B fallback into a single catalog entry so routing + fallback is simple; 2) provide a small evaluation prompt set (10–20 prompts) to run quality/regression checks post-quant. We should surface metric deltas in the report.

alice: I'll request the prompt set and the signed license snippet. @marta can you queue the scan tonight?

marta: Yep — I'll kick it now, expect report by EOD tomorrow. Quantization + validation + small eval adds 24–48h.

raju: One more infra note: if customer plans EU traffic, recommend region pinning (eu-west) to avoid extra cross-region hops — affects p95.

liam: And note: if fallback routing hits 13B often, cost math changes — sales should highlight expected qps and percent fallback to estimate committed capacity.

alice: Perfect. Timeline for customer: initial compatibility + perf report tomorrow EOD, quant & eval in 1–2 days after that. I'll update Sparrow Labs and attach our security Q answers (KMS + audit + SOC2 statement). Thanks all :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Model scan job queued: job_id=job_5612, started by marta, eta ~3h (you'll get a link when complete).
thread_summary: Sales asking eng for POC feasibility for a customer-provided 30B model: compatibility scan, quantization, latency SLO, Dedicated vs Hosted pricing guidance, KMS/VPC/audit retention, and fallback to smaller variant. Eng will run scans and deliver report.
